title: Welcome & the HTR Framework
summary: Orientation to the HTR five-pillar framework, the Equity Imperative, and your role in the health reform ecosystem.

objectives.text: Understand the HTR five-pillar framework, the Equity Imperative, and how the pillars interconnect
Describe your role in the broader health reform ecosystem
Identify the key programs and organizations you will work with

content_blocks.hint: Upload a personal welcome message from your executive director or CEO. Recommended: 3–5 minutes, MP3 or WAV.
content_blocks.label: Welcome from HTR leadership

content_blocks.body:
Health transformation is complex. It sits at the intersection of law, technology, clinical practice, economics, and social justice. New employees — regardless of their specialty — are more effective when they understand all five pillars and the Equity Imperative that tests every one of them.

This course gives you that foundation. You will not become an expert in every pillar, but you will gain the vocabulary, context, and conceptual map to work across disciplines and contribute meaningfully from day one.
content_blocks.heading: Why this course exists

items.body: Federal and state legislation, regulatory frameworks, and governance structures that define what HIEs can and must do.
items.title: Policy

items.body: Standards (HL7, FHIR), infrastructure (integration engines, MPI), and interoperability frameworks that make data exchange possible.
items.title: Technology

items.body: Payment models, value-based care incentives, and the financial levers that drive or impede transformation.
items.title: Economics

items.body: Quality measures, population health management, and evidence-based care practices that define what good health outcomes look like.
items.title: Clinical

items.body: Workforce, governance, organizational design, and the day-to-day systems that make a health reform organization function.
items.title: Operations

content_blocks.heading: The five pillars, in the order transformation has to happen

content_blocks.body: Equity is the test applied to every pillar, at every stage: is it just? Access disparities, social determinants of health, and the imperative to ensure transformation benefits everyone — not just the well-resourced.
content_blocks.heading: The Equity Imperative: not a sixth pillar

content_blocks.body: A decision about FHIR API architecture (Technology) has implications for patient consent (Policy), data completeness across populations (the Equity Imperative), care gap identification (Clinical), and cost of implementation (Economics). Always think across pillars.
